make.name: Nissan
make.description: Japanese carmaker that launched the Leaf in 2010, the first mass-market electric car. Its electric line-up now spans the third-generation Leaf, the Ariya, the Sakura kei car, the Renault-built Micra and China-only models from Dongfeng Nissan.

models.name: Leaf
models.description: The Leaf launched in December 2010 as the first mass-market electric car and was a hatchback for two generations (2010-2025). The third generation (2026 model year) is a small crossover with up to 303 miles of EPA range.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: The original Leaf hatchback (ZE0, then AZE0 from 2013), the first mass-market electric car. It started with a 24 kWh pack; a 30 kWh pack arrived for the 2016 model year.

generations.name: Second generation
generations.description: Restyled hatchback (ZE1) with a 40 kWh pack, joined from 2019 by the 62 kWh Leaf e+ / Leaf Plus. Facelifted for the 2023 model year (new Nissan logo); production ended in October 2025.

generations.name: Third generation
generations.description: All-new crossover-shaped Leaf (ZE2) on the AmpR Medium (CMF-EV) platform shared with the Ariya, with 52 kWh or 75 kWh packs, 150 kW DC charging and a native NACS port in North America. The 52 kWh base model is not sold in the US for 2026.

models.name: Ariya
models.description: Compact electric crossover built in Tochigi, Japan since January 2022. Nissan stopped US sales after the 2025 model year (tariffs and the new Leaf); it continues in Canada, Europe, Japan and other markets, facelifted for 2026.

generations.name: Original
generations.description: Nissan's first dedicated electric SUV (FE0): 63 or 87 kWh usable packs, front-drive or dual-motor e-4ORCE, 130 kW DC charging. US sales covered model years 2023-2025 only.

generations.name: Facelift
generations.description: Facelift unveiled in Japan in December 2025: grille-less nose and Leaf-style lights, Google built-in, V2L. Not sold in the US; Canada gets it with a NACS port for 2027, Germany only with the 87 kWh pack.

models.name: Sakura
models.description: Electric kei car built by NMKV at Mitsubishi's Mizushima plant since May 2022, twin of the Mitsubishi eK X EV. Japan only; 2022-2023 Japan Car of the Year; minor facelift in April 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 20 kWh kei hatchback with a 47 kW motor and 180 km WLTC range.

models.name: N7
models.description: Mid-size electric sedan developed in China by Dongfeng Nissan on the Tianyan architecture, launched April 2025 from 119,900 yuan. Exported as the Nissan Primera EV (Philippines launch November 2026); an updated N7 was due in September 2026.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Front-drive LFP sedan with 58 or 73 kWh Sunwoda packs and 160 or 200 kW motors.

models.name: NX8
models.description: Dongfeng Nissan mid-size SUV for China, on sale since 8 April 2026 as a battery-electric model (580 and 650 km CLTC) and as a range-extender (EREV, not listed here).

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: Rear-drive LFP SUV on the Tianyan architecture with 800V fast charging on the long-range version.

models.name: Micra
models.description: The sixth-generation Micra (K15, 2025) is electric-only, a twin of the Renault 5 E-Tech built in Douai, France, on the AmpR Small platform. Earlier Micras were petrol/diesel and are not listed.

generations.name: Sixth generation
generations.description: Electric supermini with a 40 kWh / 90 kW or 52 kWh / 110 kW powertrain; on sale in Europe since September 2025.

models.name: e-NV200
models.description: Electric version of the NV200 van and Evalia people carrier, built in Barcelona from 2014 with Leaf mechanicals. Replaced by the Townstar EV in 2022; never sold in the US.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 24 kWh pack at launch, 40 kWh from 2018; 80 kW motor, CHAdeMO DC charging up to 50 kW.

models.name: Townstar EV
models.description: Electric small van and Combi/Evalia people carrier, a rebadged Renault Kangoo E-Tech built in Maubeuge, France, that replaced the e-NV200 in Europe in 2022.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 45 kWh battery, 90 kW motor, 75 kW DC charging.

models.name: Juke
models.description: The third-generation Juke (F17), unveiled on 14 April 2026, is the first electric Juke; it is built in Sunderland on the AmpR Medium platform and due on sale in Europe in spring 2027. Earlier Juke generations were petrol/hybrid.

generations.name: Third generation
generations.description: Battery-electric only; Nissan has not published battery, power or range figures.

models.name: Clipper EV
models.description: Electric kei van for Japan introduced in 2024, a rebadged Mitsubishi Minicab EV.

generations.name: First generation
generations.description: 20 kWh battery, 31 kW motor, 180 km range.

legacy_notes.note: Labelled 'e-4ORCE LR Performance' (389 hp, matches the US e-4ORCE 87 kWh) but its price $39,770 is the 2025 Engage FWD 63 kWh base price and its 304 mi range is the 2023-24 Venture+ FWD 87 kWh EPA figure. EPA for e-4ORCE 87 kWh is 257-272 mi.
302 hp is the European 225 kW e-4ORCE tune, which was never sold in the US; the $54,190 price and 213 mi range match no EPA-rated Ariya. Mapped to the Europe-only 225 kW variant.
275 hp is the European 205 kW rating; the US e-4ORCE 63 kWh is 335 hp. Legacy range 158 mi is wrong (EPA 205 mi).
Range 168 mi wrong (EPA 216 mi) and price $43,190 wrong (2025 MSRP $39,770 excl. destination).
Range 233 mi wrong (EPA 289 mi for 2025, 304 mi for 2023-24 Venture+).

Second-generation Leaf SV Plus; the generation ended in October 2025 but the row is marked available. 226 mi is the S Plus figure; SV Plus was 215 mi (2019-22) / 212 mi (2023-25). Battery shown as 60 kWh (62 kWh gross).
Second-generation Leaf S (40 kWh); discontinued after the 2025 model year but the row is marked available. Legacy 'model' value contains a stray newline ('Leaf\n').
All five Ariya rows list the US in 'available_countries 2024 onwards', but Nissan dropped the Ariya from the US after the 2025 model year.

gaps: power_hp for markets that publish only kW (Europe/Japan/China variants: Ariya 225 kW and NISMO, N7, NX8, Micra, Sakura, Townstar, Clipper) is converted from the official kW/PS figure; torque_lbft likewise from Nm where only Nm was given.
Ariya pre-facelift WLTP ranges and European/Japanese prices not sourced; only EPA figures used for the original generation.
Ariya NISMO prices and ranges not sourced.
Sakura and Clipper EV yen prices not sourced (Nissan Japan site is script-rendered).
N7 CLTC range varies 510-540 km (58 kWh) and 625-635 km (73 kWh) by trim; the offering pairs the lowest range with the base price and the highest with the top price.
NX8 580 battery size and per-trim DC charging peak not confirmed; 81 kWh is cited for the larger pack only.
Leaf third-gen UK prices and Japan prices/ranges not recorded (UK range is published in miles only).
Micra 52 kWh UK price not sourced; 40 kWh price is the launch 'from' price.
e-NV200 ranges were published on NEDC/JC08, which the schema does not accept, so they are left out.

Not added for lack of a source within this run (web search budget ran out): Dongfeng Nissan Sylphy Zero Emission (China, 2018-c.2021, Leaf-based sedan), Nissan Interstar EV (Renault Master E-Tech van), Leaf NISMO (Japan, July 2026, a trim of the third-gen Leaf).
